mainTopic: Cutting nails and trimming the mustache during אבל and the מועד, the power of spoken words, and who may launder clothes on חול המועד.
overview: The גמרא rules like רבי יוסי, who allows cutting nails on the מועד and during אבל, because in אבל we follow the lenient view. A story follows about שמואל and his brother פנחס. It teaches that spoken words can come true (ברית כרותה לשפתים), with a proof from what אברהם said at the עקידה. The גמרא then clarifies that an אבל may cut both fingernails and toenails, but not with special nail scissors. From רבי יוחנן biting his nails on חול המועד, it learns three rules, and it explains why throwing nails in the בית מדרש is not dangerous. רבי allowed a mourner to cut nails and trim the mustache, and the אמוראים discuss how much of the mustache may be cut. After two side teachings about פרעה, the גמרא returns to the משנה's laundering rules. It defends רבי יוחנן's leniencies for someone with only one shirt and for linen garments. רבא begins a challenge to the linen ruling, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ruling follows רבי יוסי on the מועד and on mourning
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, both for the מועד and for אבל, because שמואל taught that in matters of אבל we follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי regarding the Festival and regarding mourning, as שמואל said: the הלכה follows whoever is lenient in mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final practical ruling: we follow רבי יוסי, the lenient opinion, about cutting nails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion debated whether cutting nails is allowed during the מועד and during אבל, and רבי יוסי was lenient. The גמרא backs this ruling with a general rule from שמואל: in any argument about אבל, the lenient side wins.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of the Festival (חול המועד)

steps.whatToRemember: In laws of אבל, we follow the lenient opinion (שמואל), so cutting nails is allowed like רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of deciding הלכה that is used throughout the laws of אבל.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei
regarding the Festival and regarding mourning,
as Shmuel said:
The halacha follows the words of the lenient one in mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier dispute about cutting nails by giving the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Cutting nails is permitted during the מועד and during אבל, like רבי יוסי, because in אבל we follow the lenient view.

steps.title: שמואל visits his mourning brother פנחס
steps.stepSummary: A relative of פנחס died. שמואל came to comfort him and saw that his nails had grown long.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something sad happened to פנחס, the brother of שמואל (a relative died). שמואל went in to comfort him and saw that his nails were long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the ruling about cutting nails. This step sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פנחס is an אבל and has not cut his nails. Since we just learned that the הלכה permits it, this detail prepares שמואל's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Something bad happened to him (a gentle way of saying someone close died)
Literally 'to ask the reason'; here it means to offer comfort

phrases.english: Pinchas, the brother of Mar Shmuel,
something happened to him,
phrases.notes: A soft way of saying that a close relative of his died.

phrases.english: Shmuel went in to ask him the reason.
phrases.notes: Asking 'the reason' here means coming to comfort him.

phrases.english: He saw his nails
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letter in square brackets, which makes it 'his nails.'

phrases.english: that they were long,

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּנְחָס אֲחוּהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל אִיתְּרַע בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that shows the ruling about nails in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story: פנחס, an אבל, had long nails.

steps.title: שמואל asks why the nails are not cut
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks פנחס why he has not cut his nails.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why haven't you cut them?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל asks his mourning brother why he is not cutting his nails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that an אבל may cut his nails, like רבי יוסי. So, in his view, there is no reason for פנחס to leave them long.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי לָא שָׁקְלַתְּ לְהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why don't you cut them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל responds to the long nails he just saw.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why פנחס is not cutting his nails when it is permitted.

steps.title: פנחס answers: would you take it so lightly?
steps.stepSummary: פנחס replies that if it had happened to שמואל, he would not treat his mourning so lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it had happened to you, would you treat it so lightly?
steps.whatsHappening: פנחס answers with a sharp reply: a real mourner would not care about cutting nails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פנחס is not arguing about the law. He is saying that a person who truly feels the loss would not bother with grooming. His words hint that שמואל might also become an אבל, and that sets up what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'with his own'; a polite way to say 'if it happened to you'

phrases.english: He said to him: If it were his own,
phrases.notes: Literally 'his own'; he means 'if it happened to you,' said politely to avoid wishing it on שמואל directly.

phrases.english: would you treat it so lightly?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A real mourner would not be so casual; if it were you, you would not cut them either.

steps.title: פנחס's words come true
steps.stepSummary: His words turned out like 'an error that comes from a ruler,' and soon שמואל himself became an אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was 'like an error that comes from a ruler,' and something sad happened to שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that פנחס's careless words came true: שמואל lost a relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a ruler whose words take effect even when he did not mean them. Here, פנחס's 'if it happened to you' actually happened. This sets up the lesson about the power of speech.

keyTerms.meaning: An error, something done by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: פנחס did not curse שמואל on purpose. The point is that even unintended words can come true.

phrases.english: It was "like an error
that goes out from before the ruler,"
and something happened to Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of פנחס's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פנחס's words came true, and שמואל became an אבל.

steps.title: שמואל throws his nails and teaches about the power of the lips
steps.stepSummary: פנחס came to comfort שמואל. שמואל cut his nails, threw them at him, and asked: don't you know that words have power?
steps.simpleTranslation: פנחס his brother went in to comfort him. שמואל took his nails and threw them at his face. He said to him: Don't you know that a covenant is made with the lips?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל shows his own practice, cutting his nails as an אבל, and scolds פנחס for his careless words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By cutting his nails as an אבל, שמואל acts on the lenient ruling. He then teaches that what a person says can cause it to happen (ברית כרותה לשפתים), so פנחס should not have spoken that way.

keyTerms.meaning: At his face, in front of him
A covenant is made with the lips; spoken words can come true

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces a well-known idea: be careful with your words, because they can shape what happens.

phrases.aramaic: עָל פִּנְחָס אֲחוּהּ לְמִישְׁאַל טַעְמָא מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Pinchas his brother went in to ask him the reason.
He cut his nails
and threw them at his face.
He said to him: Don't you hold that
a covenant is made with the lips?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל responds to פנחס's earlier words, which came true.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words have power (ברית כרותה לשפתים), and an אבל may cut his nails.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן proves from אברהם that words have power
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the source for 'a covenant is made with the lips' from אברהם, who said 'we will come back,' and both did come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: Where do we learn that a covenant is made with the lips? From the פסוק: 'And אברהם said to his young men: Stay here with the donkey, and I and the lad will go up there, and we will bow down and come back to you.' His words helped, and both of them came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from the תורה for שמואל's idea that spoken words can come true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was going to bring יצחק as a sacrifice, yet he said 'we will come back.' His words helped bring it about, and both returned. This proves that what one says can shape events.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter was helped along (his words had an effect)

steps.whatToRemember: ברית כרותה לשפתים: words have power. The proof is אברהם saying 'we will come back,' and both did.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that a covenant is made with the lips?
As it says: "And Avraham said to his young men:
Stay here with the donkey,
and I and the lad will go up there,
and we will bow down and come back to you,"
and the matter was helped along,
so that both of them came back.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּרִית כְּרוּתָה לַשְּׂפָתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the idea שמואל just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a covenant is made with the lips (spoken words can come true).
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 22:5: אברהם said 'we will come back,' and both אברהם and יצחק returned.

steps.title: First understanding: only fingernails are allowed
steps.stepSummary: People first understood from שמואל that a mourner may cut his fingernails but not his toenails.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from him: the nails of the hand, yes; the nails of the foot, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how people first understood שמואל's permission for an אבל to cut nails. This sets up the correction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל cut his nails while he was an אבל, people first limited the permission to fingernails and assumed toenails stay forbidden. The likely reason is that long toenails are hidden and do not bother a person the way long fingernails do.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from him (a first assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first assumption. The very next step overturns it, so don't take it as the final הלכה.

phrases.english: They understood from him
phrases.notes: "Him" is שמואל, who cut his nails while he was an אבל in the story just told.

phrases.english: of the hand — yes; of the foot — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story to the halacha that comes out of it: how far the mourner's permission to cut nails goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: a mourner may cut fingernails only, not toenails.

steps.title: Correction: hands and feet are the same
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן בר תחליפא says שמואל told him directly that there is no difference between fingernails and toenails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן בר תחליפא said: It was explained to me by שמואל himself: there is no difference between the hand and the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן בר תחליפא rejects the first assumption by reporting what he heard from שמואל himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit to fingernails was just people's guess from שמואל's action. רב ענן heard שמואל say outright that both are allowed, and a clear statement beats a guess.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה here: an אבל may cut both fingernails and toenails.

phrases.english: Rav Anan bar Tachlifa said:
To me it was explained by Shmuel himself:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא דְּיָד וְלָא שְׁנָא דְּרֶגֶל.
phrases.english: There is no difference for the hand, and no difference for the foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first assumption of step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was only a guess from שמואל's action, and שמואל himself said both are allowed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אבל may cut both fingernails and toenails.

steps.title: רב limits it: no nail scissors
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that even though cutting nails is allowed, using special nail scissors is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: But with nail scissors, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a limit to the permission: the nails may be cut, but not with the special scissors made for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission covers the act of cutting, not the normal, comfortable way of grooming. Using special nail scissors looks like regular grooming, so the mourner must cut his nails in a different way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
But with nail scissors — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the permission given in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting nails is allowed, but not with special nail scissors.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן bit his nails on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא saw רבי יוחנן in the בית מדרש on חול המועד bite off his nails and throw them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said: I was standing before רבי יוחנן in the study hall on חול המועד, and he took off his nails with his teeth and threw them away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an eyewitness story about how רבי יוחנן acted. The next step will learn rules from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story moves from mourning to חול המועד, where cutting hair is restricted. רבי יוחנן's action shows three things at once: removing nails, using his mouth, and throwing them away.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle days of a festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said:
I was standing before Rabbi Yochanan
in the study hall on Chol HaMoed,
and he took off his nails with his teeth
and threw them away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a related topic: nail cutting on חול המועד, told through a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: רבי יוחנן bit off his nails on חול המועד and threw them away.

steps.title: Three rules learned from the story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns three rules from רבי יוחנן: nails may be cut on חול המועד, they are not considered disgusting, and they may be thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn from this: it is permitted to cut nails on חול המועד. And learn from this: nails are not considered disgusting. And learn from this: it is permitted to throw them away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three practical rules from what רבי יוחנן did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the action teaches something. Removing the nails shows it is allowed on חול המועד. Putting them in his mouth shows they are not 'disgusting'. Throwing them shows that throwing them away is fine.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this.
Learn from this: it is permitted to cut nails
on Chol HaMoed,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם מִיאוּס,
phrases.english: and learn from this: they are not considered disgusting,
and learn from this: it is permitted to throw them away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws rules out of the story in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nails may be cut on חול המועד, they are not considered disgusting, and (for now) they may be thrown away.

steps.title: Challenge: throwing away nails is called wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the third rule with a ברייתא: burying nails is righteous, burning them is pious, and throwing them away is wicked, because a pregnant woman might walk over them and miscarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it is taught: Three things were said about nails. One who buries them is righteous, one who burns them is pious, one who throws them away is wicked. What is the reason? Lest a pregnant woman pass over them and miscarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the third rule, that nails may be thrown away, using a ברייתא that calls this wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ranks what to do with nails. Throwing them away is the worst, because of the danger to a pregnant woman. So how could רבי יוחנן throw his away? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Is that so? But it was taught:
Three things were said about nails:
One who buries them — is righteous,
one who burns them — is pious,
one who throws them away — is wicked.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא תַּעֲבוֹר עֲלֵיהֶן אִשָּׁה עוּבָּרָהּ וְתַפִּיל.
phrases.english: Lest a pregnant woman pass over them and miscarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third rule learned in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that nails may be thrown away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls someone who throws away nails a רשע, because it can endanger a pregnant woman. So throwing them away cannot be simply permitted.

steps.title: Women are not usually in the בית מדרש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן could throw his nails away in the בית מדרש because a woman is not usually found there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman is not usually found in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 13. The danger only applies where a pregnant woman might walk, and women do not usually come into the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said throwing nails away is wicked because a pregnant woman might step on them. רבי יוחנן threw his nails away inside the בית מדרש, a place where that danger is not normally present. So he did not go against the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman, here meaning a pregnant woman who could be harmed

phrases.english: A woman is not commonly found in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the place where he threw them had no real danger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to do what the ברייתא calls wicked
steps.terutzMaskana: In a place where pregnant women are not found, throwing nails away is fine

steps.title: The nails might be swept outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible problem: sometimes the floor is swept and the nails are thrown outside, where a woman could walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: sometimes they gather them up and throw them outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a side problem with its own answer. Even if no woman enters the בית מדרש, the nails could be swept up and dumped outside where women do walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks the answer in step 14. The danger seems to come back once the nails reach a public place outside. The גמרא presents this as a 'you might say' objection so it can answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, which brings up a possible objection

phrases.english: And if you will say:
Sometimes they gather them up
phrases.notes: He means when the floor of the בית מדרש is swept.

phrases.english: and throw them outside —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that the בית מדרש is a safe place to throw nails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nails swept from the בית מדרש end up outside, where pregnant women do walk

steps.title: Once the nails are moved, they lose their harm
steps.stepSummary: Once the nails have been moved from where they were first thrown, they are changed and no longer harmful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they have changed place, they have changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection in step 15. Nails that were moved from their original spot lose their dangerous power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger belongs only to nails lying where they were first dropped. Once they are swept away and moved, they no longer cause harm. So throwing them away in the בית מדרש stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They have changed, meaning they lost their harm

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's practice fits the ברייתא. Women are not usually in the בית מדרש, and nails that are later moved are no longer harmful.

phrases.english: Since they have changed place, they have changed.
phrases.notes: Once the nails are moved from where they first fell, they no longer carry the danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: New principle: moving the nails cancels the danger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Swept-out nails would still be dangerous
steps.terutzMaskana: Moved nails are changed and harmless, so רבי יוחנן's practice stands

steps.title: Scholars from חמתן ask רבי about cutting nails
steps.stepSummary: Two scholars from חמתן asked רבי about cutting nails, and he allowed it. According to this version, if they had asked about the mustache, he would have allowed that too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A pair from חמתן came before רבי. מר זוטרא taught it as: A pair from חמתן came before רבי. They asked him about nails, and he permitted it to them. And if they had asked him about a mustache, he would have permitted it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story where רבי allowed cutting nails. The story comes in two versions: one in the name of רב יהודה and רב, and one taught by מר זוטרא without those names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was about a mourner cutting his nails, and רבי allowed it. This version says the mustache never actually came up, but רבי would have allowed it if asked. That point sets up the next step, where שמואל disagrees about what actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he reports the story in this form

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
A pair from חמתן came before רבי,
And מר זוטרא teaches:
phrases.notes: מר זוטרא tells the same story without saying it came from רב יהודה and רב.

phrases.english: A pair from חמתן came before רבי,
and they asked him about nails —
and he permitted it to them.
And if they had asked him about a mustache —
he would have permitted it to them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוּג בָּא מֵחַמָּתָן לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a mourner cutting nails and trimming the mustache
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי permitted cutting nails. He was not asked about the mustache, but he would have permitted it.

steps.title: שמואל: they really did ask about the mustache
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the scholars actually did ask about the mustache too, and רבי permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: They also asked him about a mustache, and he permitted it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל tells the story differently. According to him, the mustache question was actually asked and answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, permission for the mustache was only a guess about what רבי would have said. שמואל reports that רבי actually ruled on it. Both versions agree that trimming the mustache is allowed; the difference is whether רבי said so directly.

keyTerms.meaning: And he permitted it to them

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
They also asked him about a mustache,
and he permitted it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אַף בִּקְּשׁוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שָׂפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the story in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי was actually asked about the mustache and permitted trimming it

steps.title: The mustache: from corner to corner
steps.stepSummary: אביטול ספרא, in the name of רב פפא, defines the mustache that may be trimmed as stretching from one corner of the mouth to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביטול ספרא said in the name of רב פפא: A mustache, from corner to corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains how much counts as the 'mustache' that רבי permitted trimming. It covers the whole area above the lip, from one corner of the mouth to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17 and 18 allowed trimming the mustache but did not say how much. אביטול ספרא gives a broad definition: the full width of the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: אביטול the scribe, a teacher's name

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: אביטול the scribe said in the name of רב פפא:
The mustache, from corner to corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: שָׂפָה מִזָּוִית לְזָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'mustache' mentioned in steps 17 and 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole mustache, from corner to corner of the mouth, may be trimmed

steps.title: רבי אמי: only the part that gets in the way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי limits the permission to the part of the mustache that gets in the way of eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: And only a mustache that interferes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי adds a limit. One may trim only the part of the mustache that bothers him while eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 allowed the whole mustache. רבי אמי narrows this: the permission is for practical need, so only hair that interferes with eating may be cut, not hair cut just for looks.

keyTerms.meaning: That interferes or gets in the way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. Step 19 allows the whole mustache, corner to corner, while רבי אמי allows only the part that gets in the way of eating.

phrases.english: רבי אמי said:
And only with a mustache that interferes.
phrases.notes: He means hair that gets in the way when eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the part of the mustache that interferes with eating may be trimmed

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: my whole mustache gets in the way
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that for him, the whole mustache counts as interfering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: For me, it is like a mustache that interferes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק applies רבי אמי's rule to himself. For him, his entire mustache gets in the way, so he may trim all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts the 'interferes' standard from step 20. He shows that it depends on the person: someone bothered by the whole mustache may trim it all.
steps.whatToRemember: A mourner may cut his nails and trim his mustache. אביטול ספרא allows the whole mustache from corner to corner. רבי אמי allows only the part that gets in the way of eating, and for a sensitive person like רב נחמן בר יצחק, that can mean the whole mustache.

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
For me, it is like a mustache that interferes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לְדִידִי כְּשָׂפָה הַמְעַכֶּבֶת דָּמֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אמי's rule from step 20 to his own situation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone bothered by his entire mustache may trim all of it

steps.title: How small פרעה was
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of אביטול ספרא: פרעה in the days of משה was very short, which fulfills the פסוק that God sets up the lowest of men.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביטול ספרא said in the name of רב פפא: The פרעה who lived in the days of משה was one אמה tall, his beard was one אמה, and his private organ was an אמה and a זרת, to fulfill what is said: 'And He sets up over it the lowest of men.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביטול ספרא was just quoted, the גמרא adds another, unrelated teaching of his. It is a story about פרעה's tiny height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is אגדה, not הלכה. The point is that the mighty king of מצרים was physically tiny, showing that God can put even the lowliest person in power, as the פסוק says.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, about the length of a forearm
A span, from thumb to little finger
To fulfill what is said in a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new, unrelated topic. The only link to the earlier steps is that the same teacher, אביטול ספרא, said it.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: And אביטול the scribe said in the name of רב פפא:
The פרעה who lived in the days of משה,
he was a cubit tall, and his beard was a cubit,
and his private organ was a cubit and a span,
to fulfill what is said:
"And He sets up over it the lowest of men."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked only by the speaker, אביטול ספרא, who was quoted in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרעה was tiny, fulfilling the פסוק that God raises the lowest of men to rule

steps.title: פרעה was a sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: אביטול ספרא, in the name of רב פפא, says that the פרעה of משה's time practiced sorcery, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביטול ספרא also said in the name of רב פפא: the פרעה who lived in משה's days was a sorcerer, as the פסוק says, "Behold, he goes out to the water."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching from אביטול ספרא about פרעה. This one says that פרעה was a sorcerer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that פרעה regularly went out to the water. אביטול ספרא reads this as going out to do magic there. Like the previous step, this is a side point in אגדה before the גמרא goes back to the laws of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: "Behold, he goes out to the water": the פסוק used as proof

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: And Avitul the scribe said in the name of Rav Pappa:
The Pharaoh who lived in the days of Moshe
was a sorcerer,
as it says: "Behold, he goes out to the water, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר אֲבִיטוּל סָפְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another teaching from the same speaker about the same פרעה, continuing step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרעה of משה's time was a sorcerer, as shown by his going out to the water.

steps.title: Someone with only one shirt may launder it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of people allowed to launder on the מועד. רבי יוחנן adds that someone who has only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And these may launder on the מועד: one who comes from overseas..." רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: someone who has only one shirt is allowed to launder it on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening of the משנה's list about laundering. It then brings רבי יוחנן's rule that a person who owns just one shirt may wash it on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering on חול המועד is normally forbidden. The משנה lists special people who are allowed. רבי יוחנן adds a new case that the משנה does not mention: a person with only one shirt. This sets up the question in the next step, because that case is missing from the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the יום טוב

phrases.english: And these may launder on the Festival:
one who comes from overseas.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: One who has only one shirt
is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ מְכַבְּסִין בַּמּוֹעֵד, הַבָּא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The aggadic side discussion is over. The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד.

steps.title: The משנה's list seems to leave out the one-shirt case
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי יוחנן from the משנה. The משנה lists only certain people as allowed to launder, which implies that someone with only one shirt is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: the משנה says, "These may launder on the מועד: one who comes from overseas, etc." That means these people may, but someone who has only one shirt may not!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי יוחנן's rule. The משנה gives a specific list of people who may launder, and the one-shirt person is not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge comes from reading the list as complete. If the משנה lists exactly who may launder, anyone left off the list, such as the one-shirt person, should be forbidden. That would contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying the משנה openly forbids the one-shirt case. He is drawing a conclusion from the fact that it is missing from the list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection:
These may launder on the Festival:
one who comes from overseas, etc.
These, yes,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד — לָא!
phrases.english: but one who has only one shirt, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a person with only one shirt may launder on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a list of who may launder. Leaving the one-shirt person off the list implies that he may not.

steps.title: The משנה is about people who own two garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב explains that the משנה lists people who may launder even when they have two garments that are dirty. The one-shirt person is a different case, and that is why he is not on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה: Let me explain it to you. Our משנה is talking about people who may launder even though they have two garments and both got dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב answers רבי ירמיה's challenge. He explains that the משנה's list is about a different situation from רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people in the משנה may launder even if they own two garments, because of their special situation. רבי יוחנן's case is someone who owns only one garment, and the משנה's list was never meant to cover it. So the list does not exclude him, and רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me explain it to you

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list is about people who may launder even with two dirty garments. רבי יוחנן adds that a person with only one shirt may launder it too.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said to Rabbi Yirmeya:
I will explain it to you:
the משנה permits them even though
he has two and they are dirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in step 25 and defends רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the משנה is talking about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's list covers everyone who may launder, so the one-shirt person is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about people who may launder even with two garments. The one-shirt person is a separate case, and he is also allowed.

steps.title: Linen garments may be laundered on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יעקב בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: linen garments may be laundered during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יעקב בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: linen garments may be laundered on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another lenient ruling from רבי יוחנן about laundering on חול המועד. This time it is about a type of fabric: linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally laundering on חול המועד is limited to the people listed in the משנה. This ruling adds a new category based on the material, not the person. Any linen garment is allowed, whoever owns it.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent (a message, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The intermediate days of the Festival

steps.confusionAlert: This is a second, separate ruling from רבי יוחנן. Do not mix it up with his earlier ruling about someone who owns only one shirt. That one was about the person; this one is about the fabric.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yaakov bar Giyorei sent a message
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Linen garments:
it is permitted to launder them during the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second leniency from רבי יוחנן beyond the משנה's list, after the one-shirt ruling was defended in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen garments may be laundered on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבא begins a challenge from the משנה's list of towels
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises an objection by starting to quote the משנה's list of items that may be laundered: hand towels, towels...
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection from the משנה: hand towels, towels...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is starting to challenge רבי יוחנן's linen ruling. He quotes the משנה's list of towels that may be laundered, and the quote continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מתיב shows this is an objection. רבא is bringing a source that seems to clash with the ruling that linen may be laundered. How exactly the משנה's list contradicts רבי יוחנן becomes clear once the full quote is given.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from an earlier source like a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Hand towels, the towels

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the linen ruling of רבי יוחנן from Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that linen garments may be laundered on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא quotes the משנה's list of towels that may be laundered as a source that seems to conflict with the linen ruling. The full quote and the exact contradiction continue past this point.
